amendments.normalized_body: In `nitrogen_cycle.rs`, the `monod_rate` helper now receives concentration-based substrate values but its doc comment and parameter name (`substrate`) give no indication of expected units. Add a brief doc comment to `monod_rate` and `monod_factor` noting that `substrate` and `k_substrate` must be in the same units (mg/L after the concentration migration) so future maintainers don't accidentally pass totals.

The `substrate_displacement_l` function in `geometry.rs` assumes 0% substrate porosity — the entire substrate volume is subtracted from water volume. Real aquarium substrates have ~30-40% porosity, so 60-70% of the substrate column is solid. Consider adding a `porosity_index` field to `SubstrateKind` or `SubstrateLayerState` and multiplying displacement by `(1.0 - porosity)`. At minimum, add a doc comment noting the 100% displacement assumption so dependents (especially the `water_volume_l_with_substrate_depth` callers) are aware.

The `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l` and `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_m2` conversion functions use hardcoded reference constants (20 L, 0.1 m²). If the default tank geometry changes, these constants silently become wrong. Add a compile-time assertion or comment linking these constants to the `TankGeometry::default()` values to prevent silent divergence.

crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:19 still defines `TankGeometry::water_volume_l()` as gross filled volume, and crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:56 plus crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:65 build ratio helpers on that same gross basis, while crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:177 defines `TankState::water_volume_l()` as the new canonical net-water volume. Leaving both public APIs under the same `water_volume_l` name preserves two incompatible meanings of water volume and makes future concentration/normalization code easy to wire back to gross volume. Rename the geometry-side gross helpers or move the canonical name there so callers only have one public `water_volume_l` semantics.
